rationale: Typesense is a mature open-source full-text search engine (C++17, GPLv3) with an in-memory inverted index backed by an Adaptive Radix Tree for fast fuzzy/typo-tolerant search. The codebase is approximately 69,704 lines of C++ source (src/), 39,885 lines of headers (include/), 108,080 lines of C++ unit tests (test/), plus TypeScript API integration tests (api_tests/tests/, tests/), a benchmark suite, and CI infrastructure. The DESIGN.md (DESIGN.md) confirms the core architectural decisions: in-memory inverted index with ART, token-to-documents mapping, disk persistence via RocksDB, ranking by token proximity and match count, and single-master multi-replica HA via Raft consensus. The repository has a large active community (10B searches/month on Typesense Cloud, 12M+ Docker pulls). Key relevance to a Veridian scraping pipeline extracting structured laptop specs: Typesense provides out-of-the-box typo-tolerant search, faceted filtering, dynamic sorting, federated multi-collection search, geosearch, vector/semantic search (built-in S-BERT/E-5 embedding models), conversational search (RAG), and image/text embedding (CLIP). The fuzzy-matching concern is directly addressed by the typo-tolerant ART-based index. The self-healing concern is partially relevant via Raft-based cluster HA and snapshot/restore capabilities. However, Typesense is a standalone server (not a library embeddable in a scraping script), requires running a separate daemon process, and its GPLv3 licensing would require compliance consideration for the broader Veridian pipeline. Tier B is assigned because Typesense is a high-quality, well-tested full-text search engine with direct relevance to the pipeline, but it is an external service dependency rather than a build-time library, and some concerns it maps to (self-healing) are only tangentially addressed through cluster HA rather than crawling-specific retry/selector-healing logic.
limitations: Typesense is a standalone server daemon, not an embeddable library -- the scraping pipeline must run it as a separate process or Docker container
GPLv3 license requires compliance consideration when distributing alongside other pipeline components
Raft-based clustering addresses server-side HA, not the scraping pipeline's self-healing selectors or page-level retry logic (only partial overlap with self-healing concern)
No native integration with scraping workflows -- documents must be indexed via REST API after extraction, which adds architectural complexity
The fuzzy matching is character-level typo tolerance within the search engine, not record deduplication across scraped data sources (distinct from the fuzzy-matching concern's deduplication use case)
No native browser automation, stealth, or anti-bot capabilities
